description: We are Cosmic Quest, a team of enthusiastic students interested in space, technology, creativity, and problem-solving. We aim to build an engaging Space Mission Design Game for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We welcome teammates interested in web development, UI/UX, JavaScript, game design, data visualization, research, and presentation. Curiosity, teamwork, and creativity are most important! 🚀🌌
summary:
SPACE MISSION 3D – Mission Control is an interactive 3D browser-based space mission design game developed by Cosmic Quest for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It allows players to experience the role of space engineers by designing, customizing, and simulating their own space missions.

Players can choose between Moon exploration, Mars expedition, and Earth observation missions, select launch vehicles, and build spacecraft using different components. They must manage limited resources such as budget, spacecraft mass, power generation, and power consumption while making engineering decisions.

The game features an interactive 3D space environment, spacecraft customization, real-time resource updates, spacecraft validation, animated rocket launches, simulated mission events, and a final mission scoring system.

Our goal is to make space mission planning more accessible and engaging for students and space enthusiasts while encouraging creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and interest in space exploration.
details:
How the Project Works

SPACE MISSION 3D – Mission Control is an interactive browser-based game that allows players to experience the process of designing and managing a space mission.

Players begin by selecting one of three mission destinations: Moon Exploration, Mars Expedition, or Earth Observation. They then choose a launch vehicle and customize their spacecraft using different components, including a spacecraft hull, propulsion system, solar panels, battery pack, scientific camera, communication antenna, thermal shield, and science laboratory.

Each component has associated values for cost, mass, power consumption, and power generation. Players must make careful decisions to keep their spacecraft within the available budget and payload capacity while maintaining a suitable power balance.

The game provides real-time resource updates as components are selected. Before launch, the spacecraft undergoes validation to check whether its configuration satisfies the game's requirements.

After successful validation, players can initiate an animated rocket launch and experience a simulated sequence of mission events. The game concludes with a mission report and performance score based on the player's engineering decisions.

Benefits and Impact

The project makes the fundamentals of space mission planning easier to understand through interactive gameplay. It encourages students and beginners to explore engineering concepts, experiment with different spacecraft configurations, manage limited resources, and understand how engineering decisions influence mission outcomes.

It promotes STEM education, creativity, critical thinking, resource management, and interest in space exploration.

Tools and Technologies

  • HTML5
  • CSS3
  • JavaScript
  • Three.js
  • WebGL
  • Vite
  • GitHub
  • Vercel

Creativity and Innovation

The project combines 3D visualization, interactive spacecraft customization, resource management, and mission simulation in an educational game. Instead of only reading about space engineering, players can actively experiment with mission design decisions and observe their effects.

Engineering Considerations

The game considers mission objectives, launch vehicle selection, spacecraft components, budget limitations, payload mass, power generation, and power consumption. It uses simplified fictional engineering values for educational gameplay and does not calculate real orbital trajectories or actual spacecraft performance.

Future Scope

Future improvements may include integration of real NASA planetary datasets, additional mission destinations, enhanced spacecraft models, more detailed mission simulations, and expanded educational information.
